items.text: Geometric regularity, recalled
$k$ perfect, $X$ and $S$ regular over $k$, one essentially of finite type over $k$: $X\times_kS$ is regular.
$X$ essentially of finite type: geometrically regular iff $X_{k'}$ regular for all $k'$, iff for one perfect $k'$, iff for all finite radicial $k'$. Regularity is a condition on the local rings.

Smooth over $k$ = geometrically regular and locally of finite type. Geometrically regular $\Rightarrow$ regular, with converse for all $X$ iff $k$ perfect; invariant under ground field extension; products of geometrically regular schemes are geometrically regular.
Without finiteness assumption on $X$

Equivalent: (a) for every regular $Y$ essentially of finite type over $k$, $X\times_kY$ is regular; (b) for every finitely generated field extension $k'/k$, $X_{k'}$ is regular; (d) for every finite radicial $k'/k$, $X_{k'}$ is regular. (No (c): a perfect extension need not be of finite type.) Then $X$ is geometrically regular.
Geometric regularity at a point
The same four conditions for the local rings of $X_{k'}$, $X\times Y$ at the points above $x$: $X$ is geometrically regular at $x$.
$X$ regular at $x$ and $\kappa(x)$ separable over $k$ $\Rightarrow$ geometrically regular at $x$; if $x$ is rational over $k$, regular = smooth at $x$.
Jacobian criterion
$X$ locally of finite type over $k$, $x\in X$. $X$ is geometrically regular (smooth) at $x$ iff there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ and an étale morphism
f=(f_1,\dots,f_n)\colon U\longrightarrow\mathbb E^n_k
Étale morphism: flat (and locally of finite presentation) with étale fibres, i.e. fibres are spectra of finite products of finite separable extensions of the residue fields.
Over $\mathbb C$: étale iff local homeomorphism of analytic spaces; for the Zariski topology this is not true, hence the étale topology (coverings: surjective families of étale morphisms).
Smooth at $x$ iff some neighbourhood of $x$ is étale over affine space.
$\Leftarrow$: étale over a regular scheme is regular; $\mathbb E^n_k$ is geometrically regular (polynomial ring over a field), so $U'$ stays regular after extension.
$\Rightarrow$ ($k$ perfect)
Suppose $\mathcal O_x$ regular and $\kappa(x)$ separable over $k$.
\mathfrak m_x=(f_1,\dots,f_p)\ \ (\mathcal O\text{-regular sequence});\qquad \kappa(x)\ \text{finite separable over}\ k(h_1,\dots,h_q),\ \ h_i\ \text{a transcendence basis}
Lift the $h_i$ to $f_{p+1},\dots,f_{p+q}$, $n=p+q$ = dimension at $x$; $f=(f_1,\dots,f_n)\colon U\to\mathbb E^n$.

Flatness: $\widehat{\mathcal O}_x$ is finite over $\hat A$ ($x$ isolated in its fibre, residue extension finite), the $f_1,\dots,f_p$ form an $\hat A$-regular sequence and stay regular on the module, so the module is free over $\hat A$ (power series ring); completion is faithfully flat, so $\mathcal O_x$ is flat over $A$.
Flat is an open condition (finite presentation); the residue extension $\kappa(y)\to\kappa(x)$ is separable, so $f$ is étale at $x$, hence on a neighbourhood (étale is open).
(With 1-differentials: $df_1\wedge\dots\wedge df_n$ generates $\Omega^n$.)
Consequences
The set $X_{\mathrm{sm}}$ of smooth points is open. It is dense iff $X$ is geometrically regular at the maximal (generic) points:
\mathcal O_{X,x}\ \text{artinian regular}=\text{field}\ (X\ \text{reduced at generic points}),\qquad \kappa(x)\ \text{separable over }k
For a field extension of finite type: geometrically regular $\iff$ separable $\iff$ geometrically reduced.
So $X_{\mathrm{sm}}$ is dense iff $X$ is reduced with separable residue fields at the generic points.
$k$ perfect, $X$ reduced, locally of finite type: the smooth points form a dense open subset.
Geometric normality

$X$ normal over a perfect field, $Y$ normal $\Rightarrow$ $X\times_kY$ normal (tensor product of normal rings over a perfect field is normal; reduce to the regular case: non-regular locus of codimension $\ge2$ plus a condition on associated primes).

Equivalent: (a) $X\times_kY$ normal for every normal $Y$; (b) $X_{k'}$ normal for every $k'$; (c) $X_{k_1}$ normal for one perfect $k_1$; (d) $X_{k'}$ normal for every finite radicial $k'$. Then $X$ is geometrically normal: stable under base change and products, implies normal, equal to normality iff $k$ is perfect.
